items.description: Archaeologists uncover jewellery, cosmetics and coins in cabinet sealed since eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD79 Fragments of personal objects, from makeup tools and a perfume bottle to coins and a child’s necklace, have been found tucked away in a wooden wardrobe sealed off for almost 2,000 years in the ruins of Pompeii. The artifacts provide an intimate glimpse of daily life in the ancient Roman city before it was devastated by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD79. The wardrobe was discovered in a room of a home on Via dell’Abbondanza, which was one of the most bustling streets in Pompeii.

items.title: IAEA says Barakah drone-strike response was effective
items.summary: An International Atomic Energy Agency mission to the United Arab Emirates has said that effective action was taken following the loss of off-site power to Barakah Nuclear Power Plant's unit 3 following a drone strike in May which caused a fire in a generator located outside the inner perimeter of the plant.

items.title: Philippines advances plans for nuclear power as energy demand rises
items.summary: The Philippines is working to establish the policy, regulatory and commercial foundations for its first nuclear power project, with a target of 1.2 GW of capacity by 2032 and a longer-term ambition to reach 4.8 GW by 2050, the World Nuclear Supply Chain conference in Manila heard.

items.title: Aura aims for final investment decision on Mauritania project this year
items.summary: Aura Energy Limited says it is targeting a final investment decision by the end of the year for the Tiris uranium project in Mauritania as a newly released bankable feasibility study confirms the project's economics. But Deep Yellow says current equity market conditions don't support a final investment decision for its Tumas project in Namibia during the current quarter.

items.title: Indiana considering 6 GW Candu nuclear project

items.title: Korean concern over proposed 'Made in EU' act's impact on nuclear power projects
items.summary: Progress on the Dukovany new nuclear project is continuing on schedule, but South Korea has concerns about the potential impact of the European Union's proposed Industrial Accelerator Act on non-member countries participating in the EU's nuclear power market.

items.title: Joint venture to produce HALEU in South Africa
items.summary: A joint venture between ASP Isotopes Inc subsidiary Quantum Leap Energy and South African state-owned nuclear energy corporation Necsa will develop, finance, build and operate a test bench and commercial-scale facility for the production of high-assay low-enriched uranium at Necsa's Pelindaba site.
